facts.raw_span: A woman in her 30s presented with a painful bruise on her hand
the bruise and pain had persisted despite icing and resting the area
She denied any personal or family history of bleeding disorders
An ill-defined indurated blue-green plaque was noted on the dorsum of the left hand
Radiography: Showed soft tissue swelling but were otherwise unremarkable
Magnetic Resonance Imaging: Showed a heterogeneously fluid hyperintense and T1 heterogeneously hyperintense lesion measuring approximately 1.6 × 0.5 × 2.9 cm
Mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue with extensive pigment deposition
Lesional cells were spindled, ovoid, and epithelioid, with open chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and without mitoses
Mixed inflammatory infiltrate including neutrophils, histiocytes, and foamy macrophages
Immunohistochemistry: Strongly positive for CD34; negative for S100, SOX10, HMB45, and Melan-A
Soft green-blue plaque on the dorsal hand
H&E stain demonstrating spindled cells surrounding fat globules

concepts.why: The presence of a painful bruise, soft tissue swelling, and a blue-green plaque, combined with the histopathological findings of mixed fibrous and mature adipose tissue, lesional cells with open chromatin and prominent nucleoli, and a mixed inflammatory infiltrate, are consistent with nodular pseudolipomatous fat necrosis, a rare condition characterized by fat necrosis and inflammation.
